t:
Greetings!
Not so long ago, a breakthrough discovery has opened up a pathway to a distant, unexplored Astral. This Astral lacks the familiar allods, shows no reflections of heroic adventures, and there are no clear routes of travel.
Instead it is full of bizarre phenomena, anomalies, and strange creatures that have never been encountered in the nearer layers of the Astral. Who knows what kind of danger lurks there? Demon Hunters consider it their duty to destroy any threat that might be hiding there, and they will use everything at their disposal in the pursuit of this goal.
During your travels in this distant Astral, you might meet powerful demons. Having defeated a demon, you'll be able to use an astral trap to capture its body's astral essence. You will also find unstable anomalies, either just-forming or in the process of disintegrating, and these can be captured as well.

Bring me any anomalous emanations you've collected in the far Astral and you will be able to trade them for rare items or special equipment. For each 100 killed demons you will receive a Treasure Chest, which I can exchange for Transforming Crystals or components for crafting Glyphs.

t: Hi there. My name's Dogrose the Forester. Can I help you with anything related to herbalism?

Alchemy... The greatest art! An intricate process of creating magic potions using simple herbs! Our goods can save lives or end it. Can you think of anything more useful? I certainly can't!
If you decide to join the noble brotherhood of alchemists I can sell you everything you need. A training book and tools should be enough to get any new alchemist started.

After you obtain a valuable item, you can use scissors or pliers to disassemble the item into its individual components. The quality of the item that you disassemble will determine the quality of the materials that you receive. The components are generally used by tailors and leatherworkers to make new gear.
Every time you successfully disassemble an item, your skill level will increase. At higher skill levels you have a higher chance to receive more valuable items. Finally, you should know that if your overall level isn't high enough, you won't be able to increase your disassembling skill past a certain point.

Describe tailoring? How can anyone describe a sunrise? How can anyone describe a dancing girl? They must be seen.
However, I will say something. My main clients are mages and necromancers, who need freedom, not defense, to fight. And believe me, they are all sharp dressers and don't want to wear rags! Only us tailors can solve this very important issue!
I am not afraid of competition, like some of my colleagues. And I freely sell a manual and instruments. If you will resolve to study this craft, you will need to buy them from me.
However, if you don't like tailoring, then talk to other schoolmasters. For example, Raw family, who are experts in tanning hides. You can find them in the Gibberling District.

Blacksmithing? It's a real art, believe me! You can't just wave your hammer - you need to break the material and occasionally your fingers! But if you work well, healers, warriors, and paladins will all be asking for your help!
If you want to become a blacksmith, talk to me. I have a book and some tools you can buy.

Collecting herbs is the most exciting and profitable work! Exciting because you always need to be attentive and stick your nose everywhere, to find rare herbs and roots. Profitable because alchemists are prepared to die for the ingredients that you bring them and will pay any price! This is what herb collection is all about!
Are you still thinking of something else? Don't! Simply buy a manual and equipment from me and you will have a foundation for wealth and popularity!

Are you interested in mining? Well... do you have strength to investigate fields, mountains and caves in the search of ore? Are you ready to fight with wild beasts and cruel bandits that stand between you and your rocks? Are you ready to haggle with blacksmiths, tailors and leatherworkers over prices to get as much money as possible... Hm, then maybe we'll tell you our secrets...
Ah, I can see the enthusiasm in your eyes! Well, if you're interested in what we just said then we can sell you a training manual and some tools.

Oh, you wanna be my competitor? Well I'm not afraid of you! Leather armor is in high demand by scouts, wardens, and psionicists! There's an endless supply of orders.
Now there's no point in wasting time. I have a special training book and a set of tools you can buy. They're pretty cheap, so you should buy some and get started immediately!

All of these people wandering around aimlessly are interrupting our thoughts... They think that mining is a piece of cake, but it's an art you know! And we are the masters of it!

Once a circus with merry clowns and acrobats, this place did not enjoy much popularity recently. Who would fly through the dangers of the Astral to see a performance? No wonder the isle has come to rack and ruin.

All of a sudden, three guys appeared, who called themselves "masters of dreams". They repaired the old circus building and sent out invitations to a carnival. They promise that their incredible show will fulfill people's long-time dreams and desires.

As for me, I think they are charlatans. They don't want money at all, this is very strange. Be on your guard, it can be a trap!

t:
Oh yeah, I know that island. Once I visited it on a missionary mission. You see, there's a tribe of genuinely wild goblins living at the White Mountain. Those poor bastards don't even know about the Great Nezeb! They are completely ignorant and aggressive to boot! They wanted to sacrifice our missionaries to some scaly beast, whom the locals actually believe to be a god! Sacrilege!
After the missionaries departed from the island, the Committee dispatched a squad of Punishers to teach those dirty pagans the basics of the true faith, mutual respect and worship of the Trinity Church.
I don't know what happened on the island, but I do know that the squad soon returned from the island all roughed up and pissed off like you wouldn't believe. Following this incident the island's coordinates and the data on the two Imperial expeditions to the White Mountain were classified.
However, I did hear rumors and gossip about some idol that the local hairy wildlings worship. Supposedly it was he that gave his servants the strength to repel seasoned Imperial fighters.
If you do end up traveling to the White Mountain, remember that those fanatics won't listen to reason. Brute force is the only reason they'll understand!

Why are you so interested in Zone 51, anyway? You shouldn't even know the name, Zone 51. This information is classified, if you didn't know!
Then again, seeing as you were directly involved in the events in Lab 13, I think you have a right to know the truth about the Empire's secret military base in the Kanian Archipelagos. Listen carefully, and remember - this stays between us!
Zone 51 is a military laboratory that continued to conduct research and experimenting with mental influence on mass consciousness after the Lab 13 incident. Project manager Nomarkh Sadaffee decided to fuse together psionic influence and physical modification of the body. In his view, the imperfect human system is incapable of manipulating its own consciousness to the fullest extent, let alone influence others. Therefore, he decided to combine prosthetic technologies of the Arisen with the subjects' psionic abilities. The resulting war machines, controlled by the power of thought, could have become the perfect army - untiring, resource-independent, incapable of betrayal... But it was Nomarkh Sadaffee himself who turned traitor! The latest info suggests that he's managed to destroy or subdue the entire Zone 51 security team. There's been no communication with the military base, and no one knows what's going on there.
So remember, if you see a lovely tropical isle in the Astral with dark metal hangars jutting out over the emerald jungle, landing on it could end up being the biggest mistake of your life... And quite possibly, the last!
r347700.n: Find out what happened in Zone 51

t:
The Underwater Kingdom? Nobody can say for sure whether it exists or not. I am not able to lie, so I will tell you what I know.

I heard this story from a merchant, Gardener was his name. He was a rich merchant, he was friendly with the free traders, they say that he was planning an Oligarchy.

One day it happened that Gardner's ship wandered off the caravan trail. He saw a small island, not even an island, more like a clod of land with a well and an abandoned hut. As luck would have it, the crew's water supplies were low. They dropped anchor, and Gardener went ashore to drink some water. He had barely bent over when a cold hand reached out of the well and grabbed him by the beard! A dull voice echoed from under the water: "Promise to give me that which you have, but about which you know nothing, otherwise I will drown you!"

Gardener was scared, and he immediately promised to hand over that about which he knew nothing. If you don't know it, you won't miss it! The water spirit let him go, but as soon as the merchant reached home, he started to pull out his hair. His wife met him on the threshold with a young child. The merchant was horror struck - he had promised to give his own child to the water fiend! But it's true when they say that merchants learn to count before they can read. Gardener remembered that he was last home more than a year ago, and he could see that the child was no more than a month old! The wife was unable to balance her debit and credit columns - the child was someone else's. Gardener threw out his wayward wife along with the child, and he gave his clerk, whom he had left in charge, a good beating - the child's features were suspiciously like those of the clerk. The merchant took to the drink something chronic, and drank away his fortune, down to the last copper. And he told the water spirit, when he came at his appointed time to collect his debt, that he could sing for it, and he paid him his interest in kicks and punches.

What a sad tale. If you see a small island with a well in the astral, don't think twice, throw a barrel of explosives down the well, to teach that water fiend who reduces honest people to poverty a lesson!

Cinderland... Now that little island has no other name. But at one time it was the best hunting reserve in the Empire. It is said that the Great Yasker himself loved to shoot ducks or deer in this reserve. The ranger there, Kuzmich, is a famous drinker - there were times when we drank so much that come morning we forgot which of us was the ranger and which the traveler. Hmm, those were the days... Now only charred stumps remain, with feral beasts roaming around. May that mad Arisen be cursed!
He was initially received as a welcome guest. And why not? A famous scientist decides to do some research in the quiet of the forest! They set up everything for him - a laboratory in the forest, all nice and quiet. He worked away, and the vials clinked... Then Kuzmich, kind soul that he is, decided to try and find a drinking companion. Well, I suppose he couldn't drink with the bears! He got into the habit of visiting the mage for a chat about science and a couple of bottles. And Kuzmich's booze is strong stuff! It was nothing to Kuzmich, he has a tin throat and steel liver, but the magician drank himself silly. And in a drunken fit he tore down his tower along with its foundations.
The scoundrel torched the forest! He imagined himself to be Fireborn, a Great Fire Mage, the lord of flame, damn him to hell. That was it, an end to the reserve - he really was a Great Mage, so the forest there keeps burning but never burns out, the beasts are burned but not roasted, and worst of all, the spirit of the forest, old Oakster, fell under his spell and is now in his service. Kuzmich went off the rails with grief, he doesn't recognize anybody, just drinks and drinks. I tired to reason with him, but he gave me a smack in the face and kicked me out of my hut, where there was a pack of fire wolves waiting for me. They chased me right back to my ship, and burned such a hole in my trousers, it's not funny! I was lucky I didn't have my skin burned off. So, if you are planning to visit Cinderland, which is all that is left of the reserve, don't forget to bring a fire extinguisher - believe me, the flames are still blazing away there like crazy.

I've been to this allod. It really is a cemetery, and it is peaceful, indeed. It's old Kanial burial grounds that look gloomy and sad, with dark trees hanging over swampy hollows, and mossy gravestones, and mysterious shadows and lights in the depths. I chose not to land there, just in case. You shouldn't trouble the dead, or they will trouble you!

Workshop? Yes, I've heard about it... That's one wicked place, mark my words.

They say, all kinds of sorcerers used to gather there to practice in peace and quiet. But their practices have gone too far: they started experimenting on Sparks, trapping them and transferring them to different bodies. It's like a filial agency of Tep's Pyramid! Surely, both the League and the Empire were outraged by these experiments. But the sorcerers did not really care and just threw all the objectors to the Astral.

Some devilry has been going on on that isle ever since. Those who flied by say that the sorcerers had started cutting down trees and building wooden soldiers and golems. Just think of it! What if that army comes alive and attacks our allods? Messing with Sparks has done no one any good.

Have you ever heard legends about enchanting Sirens' songs and shipwrecks caused by them? Well, those legends are real.

One of the distant allods is occupied by an Elven tribe - I can find no other way to call those savages. Astralonauts report that music and singing can be heard coming from the Sirens' Rock, and it makes ship crews rush to their own destruction. It is difficult to resist that magic, but it is possible if there is a gifted specialist on board. Or a deaf thug.

The amount of ship wrecks speaks for itself. It's hard to imagine how many fair sailors have fallen prey to those bloodthirsty creatures! What has happened to them? Were they eaten alive? By the way, the undead were also seen on that Rock...

I strongly recommend you to avoid that isle. We should have sent there a squad of Mentalists long ago and destroyed that trash from a safe distance.

Hm... I heard of a small allod, lost deep in the Astral. I've never been there actually. They say sinister things about it. Ships get lost... One friend of mine told me that when a ship approaches that island, its devices start to hiccup and the reactor boils!

And there's more. Once I met a drunken orc who claimed that once he was a cook on an Imperial trading ship, which crashed at that very allod. He spoke of the undead, of savages that eat humans, and of an ugly idol... Honestly, I didn't pay much attention to his drunken gibberish, but if you ever moor your ship to that allod, don't let go of your weapon!

Ah, Aoidoi. Their nation might be young, but their cities are impressive! New Bay is being constructed right now, but you can already tell it's going to be magnificent. Those stoneheads are brave, I'll give them that. This sector is swarming with crazy demons. I hope nothing evil will come of it.

I've heard that some demons don't want to fight and offer their friendship instead! I don't believe that. If the Aoidoi trust demons, they are more gullible than children.

We’re still not done with the damned Architects. Their main invasion was repelled, but they still dissipated across the whole world. A friend of mine told me that he sailed past an allod which once used to be green, and now its all stone. And they are there. Staring with their dead blue eyes. Ugh.

They must have reshaped the whole allod. Somebody’s got to get rid of them.

I believe you are well aware of the notoriety of this place. The patrimony of the noblest aristocrats has turned into a den of evil and the undead. Or, more precisely, that was the case until a squad of the League's daredevils got into the very depths of that hole and put an end to the curse. But what if it went differently?

The mysterious Astral is an enigmatic place. Sometimes it allows you to see what would have happened to the places you know if the events had unfolded differently. The Imperials have nothing to do in the Courtyard - they have more than enough trouble of their own. But what if Kania had been under the rule of the Empire? What if Elizaveta Rysina had sent an elite exorcist corps to the castle and the evil embedded there had gotten hold of their souls?

If you get into the reflection of the Courtyard, beware: those whom you meet there are not real priests, not Imperials and not even people. But the wounds they can inflict on you are quite real... but so are the treasures you will find in the storerooms!
r347722.n: Ask about the reflection of the Courtyard

t:
I don't think I need to tell you about Tensess Temple! After all, it was you who had to get through swarms of enemies to reveal the mystery of the gift of Light. I wish I knew what heroes like you saw there and what Tensess' Spark told you. However, a state secret remains a state secret. Instead, I'll tell you what I know about its astral reflection.

The dilapidated sanctuary in the depths of the jungle is the tomb of an ancient mage who rivaled Nezeb himself. You won't find Tensess' Spark in the reflection, but you will find lots of enemies... In this sense, the reflection is very close to reality.

You'll have to defeat five extremely dangerous enemies and a horde of demons at the top of the temple. However, the reward will be worth it! And who knows, maybe the reflection will share new secrets with you!

t: I see. So you want to play a war game? Well, be sure not to shoot yourself!
Is this a letter saying that you should visit the Spirit of Peace on Gipat?

The world, as we know it, is up to a very complicated mission. Only the best of the Sarnaut fighters will be able to deal with it. This is one of the aims of the Astral Confrontation. A trial that helps Director to find the best ones. Then they will be granted a chance to save the world... to prevent its destruction.

Have you ever heard of the Drifting Allods?
These small islands are following complicated orbits, traveling across different Astral sectors.
If you decide to capture such allod, you travel in time and appear on the allod during a certain phase of its existence. Thus, several parties may fight for a single allod at the same time in our world, but at different time periods on the allod itself.
Time for capturing the drifting allods is limited, as they are highly unstable.
The luckiest guilds will be able to take control over an allod in all its phases. It won't be easy, though.
To cut it short, capture and hold the drifting allods - this is your mail goal in the Astral Confrontation.

The beings that protect the drifting allods from the imminent Astral are not the Great Mages, although they use the same abilities. In fact, they are Director's assistants
Yes, they are able to repel Astral. The conquerors will have to fight them during the Astral Confrontation, and this battle will not be easy.
r352218.n: Ask about the Great Mages of the Drifting Allods

t:
I am the Spirit of Peace.
It often happens that the road to peace is paved with dead bodies and soaked with blood.
Ignoring the truth would be an act of cowardice. But since you received this letter and came here... I assume that you are not a coward.

Astral is the basis for everything. This is the source of any entity, primal substance in its pure form, creating and destroying things.
Astral is composed of differing layers, so far you are only familiarized with the first one. But there is also life in the faraway Astral corners.
Don't be like a blind man assured that the world is limited by the length of his stick. Throw away your stick and you will see the light.
Remember, you have a unique opportunity - you can discover all secrets of the Astral, step into its depths. But no one knows what awaits you there. One thing I'm sure of - the things that do not kill you make you stronger.

t:
You have already found four Astral Crystals.
Imperial Jade is a gem of travelers. It will protect you on your way.
Citrine is a symbol of cunning. It will save you from enemy intrigues and cheating during your journeys.
Amethyst will calm your mind.
Agate will warn you of oncoming danger.
But it's not enough to go further. You need two more gems.
No traveler will survive without a bit of luck, that's why you need Turquoise gem.
Besides, you can't continue your journey without Malachite. This gem binds the entire universe to our world.
When you gather all keys, Astral Gateway will open.
In the deeper layers you will meet much more powerful enemies. Perhaps you will find there new keys allowing you to dive into deeper layers. Take your chance and fight against the strongest opponents.
This is a challenge, a great trial. Pass the test, and you will be glorified. Fail, and no one will remember you. Choose your destiny!

t:
Have you ever been to the Vortex Isle?

An icy rock hovering in the Astral. A tomb of the Great Dragon defeated back in June times can be found there. Dragon's ghost has been guarding the Tomb for thousands of years.

There is an abundant supply of meteorite ore on the isle, so we are extremely interested in getting control over it. Perhaps you can help?

Listen carefully. In order to get to the Wraith, you will have to fight Glacier Elementals, Wild Yetis in the cave and Harpies that guard the pass to the Great Dragon's Tomb. Only near the Tomb you will be able to see the Wraith and defeat it.

I assume you already know that Imperial research in the fields of magic and science is performed in top secret labs.
However, the glorious history of our progress has one dark spot. I am talking about the Lab 9.
Yasskul Skritam, Tep cultist who follows his Master will zealously, has interfered into our experiments and revived the Plague, ancient disease that exterminated the Zem people.
Now the island is in total control of the diseased. There is no possibility to cure them. We can only bring peace to both these people and General Novikov, the head of the Lab 9 now known as Plague General. You also should get rid of infected zombies carrying the disease. And of course you should kill Yasskul Skitram who caused all troubles at the plagued island.
Can you handle it?

The Silent Hills... I used to visit them quite often. I talked to ordinary Kanian people without fear, enjoyed their delicious fresh bread. Oh what a blessed land... it was.

Now this Isle is haunted. The ghosts live lives like normal people - they fish, hunt, grind flour. But when I arrived there the last time, they were not happy to see me or my crew. We barely escaped!

I'm puzzled! What kind of evil came to Silent Hills? Who cursed these people?

If you're brave enough to challenge this mystery, follow my advice. Search the Dark Forest! This had always been a nasty place. Maybe the evil that had been sleeping there woke up! Your way there will certainly be full of danger.

Remember that you will have to fight the ghosts to cleanse the Isle. This is the pain you will have to overcome. Keep in mind that you're giving them freedom, not death.

During my travels I try to keep away from Wolf Island. There is an old legend about this death trap, a Kanian village that became a feeding ground for a werewolf.

A long, long time ago Kanian druid Vseslav the Charming got so close with the wolves from the island that he learned how to transform into one. He became their leader, and his neighbors were his first victims. After a while the whole island became infested with wolves and werewolves. Unlucky travelers who ventured to the island were eaten by predators.

If you want to perform a feat, Wolf island is just the place for it. Here's my advice: think twice before you challenge the pack!

My friend Roman Kuzin, traveler and researcher, was unlucky to get stranded on the Lost Isle. I haven't heard from him since then...

The Lost Isle has its legend. This is the legend of Tep's Pyramid that came into its own mind and started raising the undead. People say that the one who manages to conquer the Pyramid, will receive a great treasure.

Roman was dreaming of this adventure. He learned a lot about this island. I will tell you everything I know if you agree to save my friend.

On the Lost Isle you will face Magic Elementals that are spawned by the powers of the Pyramid. You will also come across a lot of undead. Destroy them to get to the Pyramid and find a way to disable it, and you will be rewarded.

So? Will you help me?

What do you know about Goblins?

On the one hand, they are just miserable creatures. Everybody makes fun of them and despises them. There are all sorts of goblin jokes, and they are also known as pets for orc shamans. Sometimes I feel pity for them.

And on the other hand, they are thieves and bandits. Scoundrels, they are always up to something evil! Have you ever met goblin weapon dealers in Coba Plateau? Then you know what I am talking about!

Goblins have their own island in the Astral. This is their citadel, their republic! They even elect a... there's one funny word for it... a President! For the third time in a row they re-elect a shaman named Urub. It's he who's responsible for goblin raids on our allods.

If you happen to find this island, enforce the death sentence to the goblin "President"!

I'd never recommend you to mess with Draconids. They are dangerous. Even Demon Hunters who forged an alliance with them don't trust them completely. Why? Because Draconids don't share their secrets to anyone! Even to their friends.

I don't know what they are hiding in their Green Maze. Historians who explored it couldn't get to its depths, the way was blocked with a magic barrier. Once they tried to get through it, two High Draconids, Border Guards as they called themselves, appeared to drive the Historians away. From that day, Draconids would always meet unwelcomed guests with steel.

If you are willing to take a risk, try to solve the mystery of the Green Maze. However, you must find the path into the ancient ruins yourself.

Have you heard the legend of the Isle of the Damned? This sad story proves that one evil soul can be worse than the whole world of evil.

Once upon a time there was a small village on some distant Astral island. Nice and honest people lived there. A loving couple was among them - Ivan and Maria, who got married and lived happily.....for a while. It should have been the perfect end of their fairy tale... but it wasn't.

A foreigner lived in that village. He was not a good one, but a man with a greedy and envious soul. He craved Maria's beauty and tried to approach her, but Maria brushed him off.

When Ivan and Maria got married he was out if his mind and decided to ruin their lives. He stole Maria's wedding ring, Ivan's love letter and a bunch of wedding flowers. He used these items to cast an evil curse on the young couple.

They went off to their graves soon and were buried together. But evil does not just vanish - an awful curse fell on the whole island and the villain himself. He died and turned into an undead.

You must find the wedding ring, the letter and the flowers, bring them to the grave and free the poor souls.
r353472.n: Ask about the Isle of the Damned

t:
I have never been to the Border Isle.

It is called like that because it often floats near Holy Land. It's not a surprise that both League and Empire fought for this allod to use it as a basecamp and to fortify their positions. We lucky enough to capture it first.

Anyway, access to the Isle is denied now. The Xadaganian garrison defending the Border Isle has betrayed the Empire! Obviously, demons cultists appeared among the soldiers. Or it may as well have happened because of the Astral worm entrenched in the middle of the Isle... They say it's able to corrupt people's minds.

Elizaveta Rysina herself has recently asked me about heroes willing to help the Empire. At the moment our army cannot afford sending an expedition to the Isle, but someone has to punish the traitors!

Have you ever heard of the Volcano Isle?

A Draconid tribe used to live on that island. They worshipped the God of Fire, who was sleeping in the crater of the dormant volcano. Sacrifices maintained his sleep and contained his rage.

But when the High Priest of the Draconids died, the knowledge of the ritual was buried with him. The volcano erupted and a powerful fire elemental escaped! He created four guards out of magma and flame - these huge manticores would turn anyone to ashes with their hot breath!

Many Draconids died, but the most cunning of them survived. They bring Crawler hearts in special bowls as sacrifices to protect themselves from fire.

If you ever try to drive the elementals back into the volcano, remember: do not attempt to attack the elemental while the manticores are alive! The God of Fire distributed his power among them, so killing the guards will make him weaker.

That's all I know. Good luck!

During one of my expeditions I was unlucky enough to visit the Tomb Isle. At first it appeared a silent and deserted place, a quiet home to one of Tep's Pyramids.

My second visit was proof of the terrible news of Tep's revived cult. Now his followers rule there. They use rock elementals to dig out the Pyramid. I don't know what they're looking for. They attacked me and my team, my people were badly wounded, so we had to leave the Isle really fast. I feel bad about it.

I'd like to ask you to find this Isle and put an end to the cultists.

In one of the expeditions I discovered an Astral isle that must have fallen apart from Holy Land. There is a Site of Power on this isle, a rich source of the Holy magic for which both League and Empire would die for.

The trouble is that the local folks have created a cult of blood around it. They are sure that the Gift of Resurrection had been brought to them by the Scorpion King, a giant creature that they call Serket. Both Waterfolks and Forestfolks strive for his grace fighting each other. They sacrifice living creatures to be devoured alive, and these poor victims can never be resurrected. But the people of this isle believe that these sacrifices ensure resurrection to the others.

This amok has to be stopped. It dishonors the idea of the Light. The Empire needs to take this Site of Power under its control! However, the waterfolks and the forestfolks are not going to have you challenge their poisonous king. You will have to fight them first. The waterfolks are the strongest, so they are going to be your primary target.

But your ultimate foe is Serket, the Scorpion King.
r353476.n: Ask about the Isle of the Poison God

t:
Maybe you have already encountered creatures corrupted by the Astral. It transforms them, usually for the worse...

Astral Horn is one of these creatures. It's a unicorn that was turned into a dangerous monster. It's not easy to find and very difficult to defeat. But I know a thing that might be helpful...

When you find the Astral Horn Isle, you will have to smash your way through the Astral crystals using the Hammer of Pain. You will get it by defeating Splasher, a fierce water elemental. You will also have to fight against Granite Trolls to find Shards of Pain. Power concealed in them can be used to charge your weapon with magic in the June Ruins guarded by a cyclops called Stomper.

With the charged Hammer, you will be able to break through the magic defenses blocking the way to Horn's den.

I'm not sure what you will find there. Be prepared to anything. I know that Astral Horn is hard to find. It's a master of camouflage.

Good luck!

Oh, you heard the rumors about this island?

A mysterious place. It's an ancient June Forge captured by Tep's cultists. Nobody knows what is happening there. I heard of a group of reckless travelers who dared to enter the depths of the ancient volcano where the Forge is located.

Only one of them came back. He said that cultists are trying to take control over ancient June machines, trying to turn them into their loyal servants. If they succeed...

The June's genius combined with Tep's insanity... Ouch... Be extremely careful if you are up to this adventure.

Who would have thought that people and vampires could live in peace? You wouldn't believe me, but there is such a place! It's called Enoch Island.

It was once a real backwater, with just two towns. Not so long ago some vampires forsook their creator, Armando de Doucer, and arrived on the island. They somehow came to an agreement with the peasants, bartering their own goods, healing magic and other useful things for blood. Everything has changed when the werewolves got to Enoch.

A vicious pack of half-wit beasts came barging in, bringing an end to the peace that the island had once enjoyed. Their chief, Luth the Meager, a former ringleader of a gang of thieves, vowed to devour anyone who failed to bow before him. The vampires protected themselves from the werewolves with a magic barrier, and closed the roads between the villages. Alongside the peasants, they have been resisting the monsters' attacks, but their strength is fading.

So if your travels happen to take you to Enoch Island, be prepared for quite a fight! Before getting at their leader, you will have to cleanse both villages of werewolves.

Yes, I've heard of that town. White-17 is a top secret military settlement, hidden deep in the Astral. As far as I know, there is something to hide! You see, Imperial scientists in White-17 were engaged in extremely dangerous research. People say that lead researcher Nomarkh Ebol maintained close relationship with Yasskul Setnakhte. Well, I've already told you about Setnakhte and the incident at the Lab Nine.
We have lost touch with White-17 a short time ago. I'm afraid they got into trouble just like General Novikov and his subordinates. So if you happen to come across the snow-covered isle guarded by Imperial soldiers, I'd suggest you to sail away. But should you decide to land, find Valentine Shtammin, a friend of mine and chief engineer there. He is smart, reliable and always ready to help. I have a feeling there is something wrong with White-17...

Once a circus with merry clowns and acrobats, this place did not enjoy much popularity recently. Who would fly through the dangers of the Astral to see a performance? No wonder the isle has come to rack and ruin.

All of a sudden, three guys appeared, who called themselves "masters of dreams". They repaired the old circus building and sent out invitations to a carnival. They promise that their incredible show will fulfill people's long-time dreams and desires.

As for me, I think they are charlatans. They don't want money at all, this is very strange. Be on your guard, it can be a trap!
r353501.n: Ask about the Carnival of Fantasy

t:
So, are you one of those interested in these events?

It was once an Imperial mine, where hundreds of goblins were gathering precious strategic resources under watchful eyes and loud swearing of our foremen. There were also natives - kobolds and mountainfolks, but they were granted a status of honorary Imperial citizens by a special decree number... what was it... 123/16, I guess... So they were obliged to work for the welfare of their new motherland.

But those scums didn't want to work! They had no idea of discipline! These lazybones didn't believe in our bright future.

They conspired with a smart goblin, Gym the Cheapskate. Trolls also joined their side, and together they managed to drive away our foremen and engineers! Now they are living as a commune under the leadership of Gym. He ordered to block all tunnels, so they think they are safe.

But every day is not Sunday! There is a group of goblin demolishers on this isle who are still loyal to the Empire. They can break through the rock to the den of separatists and plunderers.

You are allowed to punish Gym and take all his belongings. The Empire will honor you!
